styleSelection.reason: Precise architectural watercolor: sandstone planes, slate roofs and window recesses are value planes with hard edges on dry paper; ink only on the hard dark lines the target shows (mullions, recesses, signs).

families.referenceCue: Cool blues: pale cerulean-to-ultramarine sky, deeper at the top right and fading to near white above the rooflines, laid as one connected granulating wash; the same cool family holds the slate and glass, which stay on dry paper.
Blue-grey slate roof planes: one flat graded wash per plane, darker under the ridge, hard edge against the stone coping.
Warm ochre and raw-sienna sandstone: broad pale lit planes on the central gable and right wing, block pattern as light dry brush over the connected wash, never as dark dots.
Shaded stone of the left tower and left wing: greyer, cooler sandstone under one connected shadow glaze that crosses wall, windows and buttresses.
Dark navy glass in lancet and mullioned windows: dark recess accents laid last on dry paper, lit stone mullions and sills left light.
Young yellow-green street tree: one irregular canopy mass wet on dry, darker greens on its shadow side, thin trunk last.
Street level: light pavement, small figures and signal heads as small dark accents; white shirts kept light.
